originalGherkin:
Feature: Load Card Reversal
  As a Super Admin
  I want to reverse Load Card transactions (single or in bulk)
  So that any amount can be sent back to the correct PM or Corporate wallet
  in a safe, traceable and duplicate-free way, while PM Admin and Corporate Admin can
  only view the reversal reports

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Glossary (simple words used in this file)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  #   "Load Card transaction"    = the original transaction where money was loaded on a card
  #   "Reversal"                 = sending the loaded amount back from the card to a wallet
  #   "Super Admin"              = the ONLY role allowed to search, select, reverse
  #                                (single or bulk) and trigger any wallet credit
  #   "PM Admin"                 = Program Manager Admin. Owns a PM Wallet. Can only
  #                                VIEW reversal reports, cannot perform any reversal
  #   "Corporate Admin"          = Corporate Admin. Owns a Corporate Wallet, onboarded under
  #                                a PM. Can only VIEW reversal reports, cannot perform
  #                                any reversal
  #   "SR Number"                = a unique Service Request number given to every bulk
  #                                reversal request, used later to find its report
  #   "Card Ref No."             = Card Reference Number, used to identify a card
  #   "Direct PM card"           = a customer onboarded straight under a PM (no Corporate)
  #   "Corporate card"           = a customer onboarded under a Corporate, which onboarded under a PM
  #   "Other Reports"            = a new sub-section placed inside the existing Report Center
  #                                navigation, reachable as: Report Center → Other Reports.
  #                                It uses the existing report framework (same look, filters,
  #                                pagination, export behavior as other reports).
  #                                It is read-only and visible only to PM Admin and Corporate Admin.
  #   "Refund Wallet"            = the wallet that actually received the reversed amount for a
  #                                given record - always either "PM Wallet" or "Corporate Wallet".
  #
  # Status vocabulary (fixed, do not mix):
  #   - Card status can be any of: Active | Inactive | Temporary Block | Permanent Block |
  #     Stolen | Lost | Damaged
  #   - Reversal status is always one of: Success | Failed
  #   - Card status is NEVER a reason to allow/deny a reversal. Only the transaction
  #     and business rules decide that.
  #
  # Role rule (applies to EVERY scenario in this file, not just the permission section):
  #   - Super Admin is the only role that can search cards for reversal, perform a
  #     single reversal, access Bulk Card Reversal, upload/proceed/submit a bulk file,
  #     generate an SR Number, and trigger any PM/Corporate wallet credit.
  #   - PM Admin and Corporate Admin are report-viewing users ONLY. They can open the
  #     Report Center(s) and view records permitted for their role.
  #   - Super Admin performs the reversal (single or bulk) on the customer's card.
  #     PM Admin and Corporate Admin never perform the reversal; they only view the
  #     result of it, scoped to their own wallet, inside Report Center → Other Reports.

  #   - The refund WALLET OWNER (PM or Corporate) and the ACTOR who performs the
  #     reversal (always Super Admin) are two separate concepts. Super Admin performs
  #     the action; the money still lands in the correct PM/Corporate wallet.
  #   - Backend APIs must enforce Super Admin-only authorization for every reversal
  #     operation, independent of what the frontend shows or hides.
  #
  # Requirement / Acceptance Criteria map (section numbers match the source document):
  #   @REQ-1  Load Card Reversal page search (Mobile Number / Card Ref No.) - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-2  Report Center button (main report, single + bulk) - all roles, read-only
  #   @REQ-3  Bulk Card Reversal button and page - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-4  Sample Download (.xlsx template) - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-5  Bulk file upload validation - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-6  Card eligibility (status does not matter)
  #   @REQ-7  Card ownership hierarchy (Direct PM vs Corporate)
  #   @REQ-8  Single reversal wallet selection - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-9  Bulk reversal wallet selection (via Username column) - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-10 Wallet / hierarchy validation
  #   @REQ-11 Original Load Card transaction lookup
  #   @REQ-12 Reversal amount validation
  #   @REQ-13 Duplicate reversal prevention
  #   @REQ-14 Single reversal processing (atomic, end to end) - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-15 Bulk reversal processing (row by row) - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-16 Bulk confirmation popup - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-17 SR Number generation - Super Admin only
  #   @REQ-18 Bulk record independent success/failure
  #   @REQ-19 Atomic financial processing (no partial state)
  #   @REQ-20 Transaction relationship / traceability
  #   @REQ-21 Failure handling and error messages
  #   @REQ-22 Concurrency / race condition safety
  #   @REQ-23 Audit trail
  #   @REQ-24 Bulk Card Reversal Report Center (search by SR Number) - Only Super admin, read-only
  #   @REQ-25 Main Load Card Reversal Report (single + bulk together) - Only Super admin, read-only
  #   @REQ-26 Report Center → Other Reports (new navigation) - PM Admin & Corporate Admin only
  #   @REQ-27 Other Reports column set
  #   @REQ-28 Role and permission handling - Super Admin executes, PM/Corporate Admin view only
  #   @REQ-29 Backend authorization - direct API access is blocked for non-Super Admin
  #   @REQ-30 Other Reports must clearly show PM Wallet vs Corporate Wallet credit
  #   @REQ-31 Other Reports data scope per role
  #   @REQ-32 Other Reports is read-only (no action controls)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  Background:
    Given "Super Admin" is the only role authorized to perform reversal actions
    And "Maximize Admin" is a PM Admin who owns a PM Wallet and is a report-viewing user only
    And "Alpha Corp Admin" is a Corporate Admin who onboarded under "Maximize Admin", owns a Corporate Wallet, and is a report-viewing user only
    And the customer with mobile number "9937894322" has a Gift Card directly onboarded under "Maximize Admin"
    And the customer with mobile number "9937894322" has a GPR Card onboarded under "Alpha Corp Admin"
    And each card has one successful Load Card transaction that has not been reversed yet

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Load Card Reversal Page - Search (Super Admin only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-1 @search @super-admin
  Scenario: Super Admin searches by Card Reference Number and gets the matching card
    Given "Super Admin" is logged in to the Load Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" searches by the Card Reference Number of the Gift Card
    Then only that Gift Card should be shown in the result

  @REQ-1 @search @negative
  Scenario: Super Admin search with an unknown mobile number returns no cards
    Given "Super Admin" is logged in to the Load Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" searches by mobile number "9900000000"
    Then the search should return no cards
    And a message should say that no card was found

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Report Center Button (main report) - all roles, read-only
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-2 @report-center
  Scenario: Report Center button opens the main Load Card Reversal report
    Given "Super Admin" is on the Load Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" clicks "Report Center"
    Then the Load Card Reversal report should open
    And the report should show these columns:
      | Mobile Number | Card Reference Number | Status | Status Description | Amount | Processed/Created Time | Updated Time |

  @REQ-2 @REQ-25 @report-center
  Scenario: Main report shows both single and bulk reversal records together
    Given a single reversal was completed by "Super Admin" for the Gift Card
    And a bulk reversal was completed by "Super Admin" for the GPR Card under SR Number "SR100234"
    When "Super Admin" opens the Load Card Reversal "Report Center"
    Then the report should list the single reversal record
    And the report should also list the bulk reversal record
    And the bulk reversal record should still be internally linked to SR Number "SR100234"
    But the SR Number column should not be shown on this report

  @REQ-2 @REQ-28 @permission @report-center
  Scenario Outline: Report Center follows the existing role permissions for all three roles
    Given "<actor>" is logged in
    When "<actor>" opens the Load Card Reversal "Report Center"
    Then "<actor>" should only see reversal records permitted for their role
    And "<actor>" should only be able to view, not perform, any reversal action

    Examples:
      | actor              |
      | Super Admin        |
      | Maximize Admin     |
      | Alpha Corp Admin   |

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 3. Bulk Card Reversal Button and Page (Super Admin only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-3 @bulk @navigation @super-admin
  Scenario: Bulk Card Reversal button opens the dedicated bulk reversal page for Super Admin
    Given "Super Admin" is on the Load Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" clicks "Bulk Card Reversal"
    Then the Bulk Card Reversal page should open
    And the page should show "Sample Download", "Upload", "Proceed" and "Report Center"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Sample Download (Super Admin only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-4 @bulk @template @super-admin
  Scenario: Super Admin's Sample Download gives an xlsx file with the correct columns
    Given "Super Admin" is on the Bulk Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" clicks "Sample Download"
    Then a file in ".xlsx" format should be downloaded
    And the file should contain exactly these columns:
      | Mobile No. | Card Ref No. | Username | Amount |

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Bulk File Upload Validation (Super Admin only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-5 @bulk @upload @negative @super-admin
  Scenario Outline: Uploaded file from Super Admin is rejected when basic format checks fail
    Given "Super Admin" is on the Bulk Card Reversal page
    When "Super Admin" uploads a file with problem "<problem>"
    Then the upload should be rejected
    And an error message about "<problem>" should be shown

    Examples:
      | problem                     |
      | wrong file extension        |
      | missing required column     |
      | column order changed        |
      | empty file                  |

  @REQ-5 @bulk @upload @negative @super-admin
  Scenario Outline: Backend validates every row Super Admin uploads, not just the frontend
    Given "Super Admin" uploads a bulk reversal file with a row having "<row_problem>"
    When the file is validated on the backend
    Then that row should be marked invalid with reason "<row_problem>"
    And a frontend-only check should never be treated as the final validation

    Examples:
      | row_problem                       |
      | invalid mobile number             |
      | card reference number not found   |
      | invalid username                  |
      | invalid amount                    |

  @REQ-5 @REQ-28 @bulk @upload @negative @permission
  Scenario Outline: PM Admin and Corporate Admin cannot upload a bulk reversal file
    Given "<actor>" is logged in
    When "<actor>" attempts to upload a bulk reversal file
    Then the action should be rejected with an "unauthorized" error
    And no file should be processed

    Examples:
      | actor              |
      | Maximize Admin      |
      | Alpha Corp Admin    |

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Card Eligibility - status does not matter (Super Admin only performs it)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-6 @eligibility @super-admin
  Scenario Outline: A reversal by Super Admin is allowed no matter what the card status is
    Given the Gift Card status is "<card_status>"
    And the Gift Card has a valid, unreversed Load Card transaction
    When "Super Admin" reverses the Gift Card load transaction
    Then the reversal should be processed based on the transaction, not the card status
    And the reversal should succeed

    Examples:
      | card_status      |
      | Active           |
      | Inactive         |
      | Temporary Block  |
      | Permanent Block  |
      | Stolen           |
      | Lost             |
      | Damaged          |

  @REQ-6 @eligibility @negative @super-admin
  Scenario: A reversal is still rejected when the transaction itself is not valid, even if the card is Active
    Given the Gift Card status is "Active"
    And the Gift Card has no Load Card transaction on record
    When "Super Admin" attempts to reverse the Gift Card
    Then the reversal should be rejected with an "original load transaction not found" error

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Card Ownership Hierarchy (unchanged, decides the wallet, not the actor)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-7 @hierarchy
  Scenario: A card onboarded directly under a PM can only go back to that PM Wallet
    Given the Gift Card is onboarded directly under "Maximize Admin"
    When the system checks the reversal destinations for the Gift Card
    Then "Maximize Admin PM Wallet" should be the only allowed destination
    And no Corporate Wallet should be offered as a destination

  @REQ-7 @hierarchy
  Scenario: A card onboarded under a Corporate can go back to the Corporate Wallet or the Parent PM Wallet
    Given the GPR Card is onboarded under "Alpha Corp Admin"
    And "Alpha Corp Admin" sits under parent PM "Maximize Admin"
    When the system checks the reversal destinations for the GPR Card
    Then "Alpha Corp Admin Corporate Wallet" should be an allowed destination
    And "Maximize Admin PM Wallet" should also be an allowed destination

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 8. Single Reversal Wallet Selection (Super Admin picks, PM/Corp only receive)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-8 @wallet-selection @super-admin
  Scenario: Direct PM card only shows PM Wallet as a choice for Super Admin
    Given "Super Admin" has selected the Gift Card for single reversal
    When "Super Admin" opens the wallet selection
    Then only "PM Wallet" should be available to choose

  @REQ-8 @wallet-selection @super-admin
  Scenario Outline: Corporate card allows Super Admin to choose between PM Wallet or Corporate Wallet
    Given "Super Admin" has selected the GPR Card for single reversal
    When "Super Admin" chooses "<wallet_choice>" as the refund wallet
    Then the choice should be accepted because it belongs to the correct hierarchy

    Examples:
      | wallet_choice     |
      | PM Wallet         |
      | Corporate Wallet   |

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 9. Bulk Reversal Wallet Selection via Username (Super Admin processes)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-9 @bulk @wallet-selection @super-admin
  Scenario: Username in the file decides the PM Wallet as destination
    Given "Super Admin" uploaded a bulk file with a row for the Gift Card and Username "Maximize Admin"
    When the row is processed by "Super Admin"
    Then the reversal amount should be credited to "Maximize Admin PM Wallet"

  @REQ-9 @bulk @wallet-selection @super-admin
  Scenario: Username in the file decides the Corporate Wallet as destination
    Given "Super Admin" uploaded a bulk file with a row for the GPR Card and Username "Alpha Corp Admin"
    When the row is processed by "Super Admin"
    Then the reversal amount should be credited to "Alpha Corp Admin Corporate Wallet"

  @REQ-9 @bulk @wallet-selection @negative @super-admin
  Scenario: An unrelated Username in the file is rejected
    Given "Super Admin" uploaded a bulk file with a row for the Gift Card and Username "Unrelated Corp Admin"
    When the row is processed by "Super Admin"
    Then the row should fail with reason "unauthorized wallet"
    And no amount should be credited to "Unrelated Corp Admin"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 10. Wallet Validation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-10 @wallet-validation @negative @super-admin
  Scenario: Super Admin cannot manually give an unrelated PM or Corporate and let it receive money
    Given "Super Admin" attempts a single reversal for the Gift Card
    When "Super Admin" tries to set the refund wallet to a Corporate that is not linked to this card
    Then the request should be rejected with an "invalid wallet destination" error
    And the frontend dropdown restriction alone should not be relied on

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 11. Original Load Transaction
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-11 @original-transaction @super-admin
  Scenario: The system finds the original load transaction before Super Admin reverses it
    Given the Gift Card has one successful Load Card transaction of amount "500"
    When "Super Admin" reverses the Gift Card
    Then the system should find that Load Card transaction first
    And the reversible amount should be based on that transaction

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 12. Reversal Amount
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-12 @amount @negative @super-admin
  Scenario Outline: Invalid reversal amounts attempted by Super Admin are rejected
    Given the Gift Card has a Load Card transaction with reversible amount "500"
    When "Super Admin" tries to reverse an amount of "<attempted_amount>"
    Then the reversal should be rejected with reason "<reason>"

    Examples:
      | attempted_amount | reason                              |
      | 0                 | invalid reversal amount             |
      | -100              | invalid reversal amount             |
      | 900               | amount greater than reversible amount |

  @REQ-12 @amount @super-admin
  Scenario: A matching reversal amount from Super Admin is accepted
    Given the Gift Card has a Load Card transaction with reversible amount "500"
    When "Super Admin" reverses an amount of "500"
    Then the reversal should be accepted

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 13. Duplicate Reversal Prevention
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-13 @duplicate @negative @super-admin
  Scenario: A transaction that is already reversed cannot be reversed again
    Given the Gift Card's Load Card transaction has already been successfully reversed
    When "Super Admin" attempts to reverse the same transaction again
    Then the reversal should be rejected
    And the message should say "This load card transaction has already been reversed."

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 14. Single Reversal Processing (end to end, Super Admin only)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-14 @single @processing @super-admin
  Scenario: A complete single reversal is processed successfully by Super Admin
    Given "Super Admin" has selected the Gift Card with a valid, unreversed Load Card transaction
    When "Super Admin" confirms the single reversal to "Maximize Admin PM Wallet"
    Then the card/load balance should be reversed
    And "Maximize Admin PM Wallet" should be credited with the reversal amount
    And a reversal transaction should be created and linked to the original transaction
    And the reversal status should be "Success"
    And the reversal should appear in the Load Card Reversal report

  @REQ-14 @REQ-28 @single @processing @negative @permission
  Scenario Outline: PM Admin and Corporate Admin cannot perform a single reversal even for their own card
    Given "<actor>" is logged in
    And a card belongs within "<actor>"'s own scope with a valid, unreversed Load Card transaction
    When "<actor>" attempts to perform a single reversal on that card
    Then the action should be rejected with an "unauthorized, Super Admin only" error
    And no card/load balance change should happen
    And no wallet should be credited

    Examples:
      | actor              |
      | Maximize Admin      |
      | Alpha Corp Admin    |

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

requirementText: This file describes a feature where a Super Admin can undo (reverse) any amount that was loaded onto a card, and send it back to the right wallet. Only this Super Admin can search for cards, reverse payments (one at a time or in bulk using a file upload), and move money to a wallet — other users like PM Admin and Corporate Admin can only look at reports, not make changes. It doesn't matter if the card is active, blocked, or lost etc. — reversal depends only on whether there's a valid original transaction. If a card belongs directly to a PM, the money goes back to that PM's wallet; if it belongs to a Corporate under a PM, the money can go to either the Corporate's wallet or the PM's wallet. The system makes sure the same transaction can't be reversed twice, checks that amounts are correct, and prevents problems if two reversal attempts happen at the same time. Every action (successful or failed) is fully recorded for tracking and safety, and even the backend double-checks that only the Super Admin is allowed to do this, so no one can bypass the rules. Finally, there are separate report screens: one general report for super admin, one specific to bulk reversals, and a simple, view-only report for PM/Corporate Admins that only shows their own money-related records.

originalGherkin:
Feature: Card Block & Customer Deactivation
  As a Program Manager (PM) Admin / Corporate and Issuer
  I want to block cards or customers at different levels
  So that fraudulent or risky cards/customers can be temporarily or permanently
  deactivated without impacting unrelated cards, PMs/corporate, or customer

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Glossary (entity naming used consistently throughout this file)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  #   "Maximize" / "Akiko"   = Program Manager (PM) names; also the customer-portal
  #                            brand name for that PM
  #   "Maximize Admin" /
  #   "Akiko Admin"          = the PM-level admin persona who manages cards/customers
  #                            under that PM. Can only ever place a Temporary block,
  #                            and only within their own PM's scope.
  #   "Issuer"                = highest authority; can view and block across all PMs,
  #                            and may place either a Temporary or a Permanent block.
  #   "Corporate Admin"      = Corporate Admin directly onboards customers under itself. 
  #                            For blocking a card or deactivating a customer, Corporate 
  #                            Admin follows the exact same rule as PM Admin: can only 
  #                            ever place a Temporary block, and only within its own scope 
  #                            (i.e. the customers/cards it has onboarded).
  #
  # Status vocabulary (fixed, do not mix):
  #   - Card entity status      -> "Active" | "Blocked"
  #   - Customer entity status  -> "Active" | "Deactivated"
  #   - Action verbs "block(s)/blocked" and "unblock(s)" are used generically for
  #     both card-level and customer-level actions; only the resulting STATUS
  #     value differs by entity type (see above).
  #
  # Requirement:
  #   Scenarios are tagged with the @REQ-x of the requirement they satisfy. Section
  #   numbering (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7) intentionally mirrors the source requirement
  #   document, which itself has no "section 3".
  #
  #   @REQ-1 Card-Level Blocking
  #     AC-1.1: PM Admin can temporarily block a card within their own PM scope
  #     AC-1.2: An unauthenticated actor cannot block a card
  #     AC-1.3: PM Admin cannot block a card outside their own PM scope
  #     AC-1.4: PM Admin can only apply a Temporary block, never Permanent
  #     AC-1.5: Blocking an already-Blocked card is rejected; existing block is unchanged
  #     AC-1.6: Customer portal reflects each PM's card block status independently
  #     AC-1.7: Customer cannot unblock a temporarily blocked card themselves
  #
  #   @REQ-2 Customer-Level Deactivation
  #     AC-2.1: PM Admin can temporarily deactivate a customer within their own PM scope
  #     AC-2.2: PM Admin cannot deactivate a customer belonging to another PM
  #     AC-2.3: A Deactivated customer cannot log in to that PM's customer portal
  #     AC-2.4: A Deactivated customer cannot use any card under that PM
  #     AC-2.5: A Deactivated customer cannot self-unblock, Temporary or Permanent
  #     AC-2.6: Deactivating an already-Deactivated customer is rejected; block is unchanged
  #     AC-2.7: Customer deactivation is never reversible, by anyone, regardless of type (see also @REQ-7)
  #
  #   @REQ-4 Issuer Level
  #     AC-4.1: Issuer can view a customer's cards and block status across multiple PMs
  #     AC-4.2: Issuer search for a non-existent mobile number returns no results
  #     AC-4.3: Issuer can select a PM and block specific card(s) Temporarily
  #     AC-4.4: Issuer can block specific card(s) Permanently
  #     AC-4.5: Issuer can escalate a PM-placed Temporary block to Permanent
  #     AC-4.6: Issuer can deactivate the complete customer across all PMs, Temporary or Permanent
  #     AC-4.7: Issuer can block cards across different PMs independently
  #
  #   @REQ-5 Multi-PM Isolation
  #     AC-5.1: Blocking a card under one PM does not affect cards under another PM
  #     AC-5.2: Deactivating a customer with zero cards under the acting PM succeeds, no cards affected
  #     AC-5.3: A PM Admin's customer-level deactivate only applies within that PM's own scope
  #     AC-5.4: Only an Issuer-level deactivate affects the customer across all PMs
  #
  #   @REQ-6 Portal Access for Multiple PMs
  #     AC-6.1: Customer has a separate portal login/access for each Program Manager
  #     AC-6.2: Each PM's portal displays only that PM's own cards
  #     AC-6.3: A card block under one PM is reflected only in that PM's own portal
  #     AC-6.4: Customer can still access an unaffected PM's portal normally after a block/deactivate elsewhere
  #
  #   @REQ-7 Blocking Authority
  #     AC-7.1: Only the Issuer can apply a Permanent block; PM Admin is restricted to Temporary
  #     AC-7.2: A Temporary block can be unblocked by the placing PM Admin or the Issuer
  #     AC-7.3: A Temporary block cannot be unblocked by a different PM Admin or by the customer
  #     AC-7.4: If the Issuer placed the Temporary block, only the Issuer can unblock it
  #     AC-7.5: A Permanent block can never be unblocked by anyone, including the Issuer
  #     AC-7.6: A Permanent block can never be downgraded to Temporary, by anyone
  #     AC-7.7: The customer can never unblock a card or account themselves, regardless of block type
  #     AC-7.8: Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  Background:
    Given the customer with mobile number "9937894322" exists in the system
    And the customer has 10 gift cards onboarded under "Maximize Admin"
    And the customer has 1 GPR card onboarded under "Akiko Admin"
    And all cards are currently "Active"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 0. Production Data Fix: AKIKOADMIN block must not affect MAXIMIZEADMIN
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Context: The below customers were onboarded under both AKIKOADMIN (GPR Card)
  # and MAXIMIZEADMIN (Gift Card). Per client request they were blocked under
  # AKIKOADMIN, but this incorrectly also blocked them under MAXIMIZEADMIN,
  # preventing login and Gift Card usage there. Fix: the customer must remain
  # blocked only under AKIKOADMIN and must remain/become Active under
  # MAXIMIZEADMIN. Going forward, blocking under one PM must never impact the
  # customer's status under any other PM (see also @REQ-5 Multi-PM Isolation).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @production-fix @customer-level
  Scenario Outline: Customer blocked under AKIKOADMIN remains active and unaffected under MAXIMIZEADMIN
    Given the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" is onboarded under "Akiko Admin" with a GPR Card
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" is onboarded under "Maximize Admin" with a Gift Card
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" has been blocked under "Akiko Admin"
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" was incorrectly also blocked under "Maximize Admin"
    When the customer's status under "Maximize Admin" is corrected to "Active"
    Then the customer status under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Blocked"
    And the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should be "Active"
    And the customer should be able to log in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    And the customer should be able to use their assigned Gift Card under "Maximize Admin" without any issues
    And the customer should not be able to log in to the "Akiko" customer portal

    Examples:

      | 6203740710    |
      | 9768167268    |
      | 9958812998    |

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @production-fix @customer-level
  Scenario: Blocking a customer under one Program Manager must never impact their status under another Program Manager
    Given a customer is onboarded under both "Akiko Admin" and "Maximize Admin"
    When "Akiko Admin" blocks the customer within its own scope
    Then the customer status under "Akiko Admin" should be "Blocked"
    And the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"
    And the customer should be able to log in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    And the customer should be able to use any cards assigned under "Maximize Admin"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-1 @card-level @pm-admin

    And the block type should be "Temporary"
    And the blocking authority recorded should be "Akiko Admin"
    And the 10 gift cards under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @REQ-7 @card-level @negative @auth
  Scenario: An unauthenticated actor cannot block a card

    When an unauthenticated request attempts to block the GPR card belonging to mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the action should be rejected with an "authentication required" error

  @REQ-1 @card-level @pm-admin
  Scenario: PM Admin cannot block a card that does not belong to them
    Given "Maximize Admin" is logged in
    When "Maximize Admin" attempts to block the GPR card onboarded under "Akiko Admin"
    Then the action should be rejected with an "unauthorized card access" error
    And the GPR card status should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @REQ-7 @card-level @pm-admin @negative
  Scenario: PM Admin cannot apply a permanent block - only temporary is allowed
    Given "Akiko Admin" is logged in
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to block the GPR card with block type "Permanent"

  Scenario: Blocking a card that is already Blocked does not change its existing block

    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"
    And a message should indicate that only "Akiko Admin" or the Issuer can lift this block

  # 2. Customer-Level Deactivation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @pm-admin

  Scenario: Issuer selects a Program Manager and blocks specific card(s) temporarily

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @card-level @permanent-block

    Given the Issuer is logged in
    And the Issuer has selected mobile number "9937894322"
    When the Issuer selects Program Manager "Akiko Admin"
    And the Issuer selects the GPR card under "Akiko Admin"
    And the Issuer blocks the selected card with block type "Permanent"
    Then the GPR card should have status "Blocked"
    And the block type for the GPR card should be "Permanent"

  @REQ-4 @REQ-7 @issuer-level @permanent-block

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @card-level
  Scenario Outline: Issuer blocks cards across different Program Managers independently
    Given the Issuer is logged in

    And the Issuer blocks all cards under "<program_manager>"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Multi-PM Isolation Rule
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation
  Scenario: Blocking a card under one PM does not affect cards under another PM
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894322"
    And "Akiko Admin" manages 1 card for the same mobile number
    When "Maximize Admin" blocks one of its 10 gift cards
    Then that card under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the remaining 9 cards under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Active"
    And "Akiko Admin" should be able to continue normal operations on its card

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @edge-case
  Scenario: Deactivating a customer who has no cards onboarded under the acting PM succeeds with zero cards affected
    Given the customer with mobile number "9937894300" exists in the system
    And the customer has 0 cards onboarded under "Maximize Admin"
    When "Maximize Admin" deactivates the customer within its own scope
    Then the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should be "Deactivated"
    And no cards should be affected, since none exist under "Maximize Admin"

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @customer-level
  Scenario: Customer-level deactivate by one PM only applies within that PM's scope
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894300"
    And "Akiko Admin" manages 1 card for the same mobile number
    When "Maximize Admin" deactivates the customer within its own scope
    Then all 10 cards under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Active"

  Scenario: Only an Issuer-level deactivate affects the customer across all PMs
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894322"

    When the Issuer deactivates the complete customer/mobile number
    Then all 10 cards under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should have status "Blocked"

  # 6. Customer Portal Access for Multiple Program Managers
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm
  Scenario: Customer has separate portal logins for each Program Manager
    Given the customer is onboarded under both "Maximize Admin" and "Akiko Admin"
    When the customer's portal accounts are provisioned

    And the customer should have a separate login/access for the "Akiko" customer portal

  Scenario: A card blocked under Akiko is reflected in the Akiko portal
    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR Card

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm @card-level

    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR Card

    Given the GPR Card under "Akiko" has been blocked

  Scenario Outline: Each Program Manager's portal reflects only that PM's card status
    Given "<pm>" card status is "<status>"
    When the customer logs in to the "<pm>" customer portal
    Then the portal should display the "<pm>" card(s) with status "<status>"
    And the portal should not display or be influenced by any other Program Manager's card status

    Examples:

      | Akiko    | Blocked |
      | Maximize | Active  |


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Blocking Authority: who can BLOCK vs who can UNBLOCK
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Block placement rule:
  #   - PM Admin can only ever place a "Temporary" block (card or customer level),
  #     and only for cards/customers within their own PM's scope.
  #   - Issuer can place either a "Temporary" or a "Permanent" block/deactivate (card or customer
  #     level), and may escalate an existing Temporary block to Permanent.
  #
  # Unblock rule:
  #   - Temporary block:
  #       -> can be unblocked by the SAME PM Admin who placed it, OR by the Issuer.
  #       -> cannot be unblocked by a different PM Admin, or by the customer.
  #       -> if the Issuer placed the temporary block, only the Issuer can unblock it
  #          (a PM Admin cannot undo an Issuer-placed block).
  #   - Permanent block (Issuer only):
  #       -> can NEVER be unblocked by anyone, including the Issuer.
  #   - The customer can NEVER unblock anything themselves, regardless of level or
  #     block type.
  #   - Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op.
  #   - Customer/mobile-number deactivation is NEVER reversible, regardless of
  #     deactivate type (Temporary or Permanent) or who attempts it (PM Admin or
  #     Issuer). This differs from card-level temporary blocks, which ARE reversible
  #     by the placing PM Admin or the Issuer. Do not assume the card unblock
  #     pattern carries over to customer-level deactivation.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario Outline: Only the Issuer can apply a permanent block; PM Admin is restricted to temporary
    Given "<actor>" is logged in
    When "<actor>" attempts to block "<target>" with block type "<block_type>"
    Then the action should be "<result>"

    Examples:
      | actor          | target            | block_type | result   |
      | Akiko Admin    | a card            | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Akiko Admin    | a card            | Permanent  | Rejected |
      | Maximize Admin | complete customer | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Maximize Admin | complete customer | Permanent  | Rejected |
      | Issuer         | a card            | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | a card            | Permanent  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | complete customer | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | complete customer | Permanent  | Allowed  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario Outline: A card temporarily blocked by Akiko Admin can be unblocked by Akiko Admin or the Issuer
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "<actor>" unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should be "Active"

    Examples:
      | actor       |
      | Akiko Admin |
      | Issuer      |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: A card temporarily blocked by Akiko Admin cannot be unblocked by anyone else
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to unblock the GPR card
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | attempted_by              |
      | Maximize Admin            |
      | the customer (via portal) |

  @REQ-2 @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: A deactivated customer can never be reactivated, regardless of deactivate type or who attempts it
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "<deactivated_by>" with deactivate type "<deactivate_type>"
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to reactivate mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the action should be rejected with a "customer deactivation cannot be reversed" error
    And the customer status should remain "Deactivated"

    Examples:
      | deactivated_by | deactivate_type | attempted_by |
      | Akiko Admin    | Temporary       | Akiko Admin  |
      | Akiko Admin    | Temporary       | Issuer       |
      | Issuer         | Permanent       | Issuer       |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario: A PM Admin cannot unblock a card that the Issuer temporarily blocked
    Given the Issuer has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to unblock the GPR card
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario: The Issuer can unblock a card that the Issuer temporarily blocked
    Given the Issuer has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When the Issuer unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should be "Active"

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative @permanent-block
  Scenario Outline: A permanently blocked card or customer can never be unblocked by anyone
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is permanently blocked by the Issuer
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to unblock "<target>"
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And "<target>" should remain permanently "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | target             | attempted_by |
      | a single card      | Issuer       |
      | a single card      | Akiko Admin  |
      | a single card      | the customer |
      | complete customer  | Issuer       |
      | complete customer  | Akiko Admin  |
      | complete customer  | the customer |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: The customer can never unblock a card or account themselves, regardless of block type
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is "Blocked" with block type "<block_type>"
    And the customer is logged in to the relevant customer portal
    When the customer attempts to unblock "<target>"
    Then the unblock action should be denied in all cases

    Examples:
      | target             | block_type |
      | a single card      | Temporary  |
      | a single card      | Permanent  |
      | complete customer  | Temporary  |
      | complete customer  | Permanent  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative @permanent-block
  Scenario Outline: A permanent block can never be downgraded to Temporary by anyone, including the Issuer
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is permanently blocked by the Issuer
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to change "<target>" block type to "Temporary"
    Then the action should be rejected with a "permanent block cannot be reversed" error
    And "<target>" should remain permanently "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | target             | attempted_by |
      | a single card      | Issuer       |
      | a single card      | Akiko Admin  |
      | complete customer  | Issuer       |
      | complete customer  | Akiko Admin  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @idempotency @edge-case
  Scenario: Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op
    Given the GPR card status is "Active"
    When "Akiko Admin" unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should remain "Active"
    And no error should be raised

improvedGherkin:
Feature: Card Block & Customer Deactivation
  As a Program Manager (PM) Admin / Corporate and Issuer
  I want to block cards or customers at different levels
  So that fraudulent or risky cards/customers can be temporarily or permanently
  deactivated without impacting unrelated cards, PMs/corporate, or customer

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Glossary (entity naming used consistently throughout this file)
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  #   "Maximize" / "Akiko"   = Program Manager (PM) names; also the customer-portal
  #                            brand name for that PM
  #   "Maximize Admin" /
  #   "Akiko Admin"          = the PM-level admin persona who manages cards/customers
  #                            under that PM. Can only ever place a Temporary block,
  #                            and only within their own PM's scope.
  #   "Issuer"                = highest authority; can view and block across all PMs,
  #                            and may place either a Temporary or a Permanent block.
  #   "Corporate Admin"      = Corporate Admin directly onboards customers under itself. 
  #                            For blocking a card or deactivating a customer, Corporate 
  #                            Admin follows the exact same rule as PM Admin: can only 
  #                            ever place a Temporary block, and only within its own scope 
  #                            (i.e. the customers/cards it has onboarded).
  #
  # Status vocabulary (fixed, do not mix):
  #   - Card entity status      -> "Active" | "Blocked"
  #   - Customer entity status  -> "Active" | "Deactivated"
  #   - Action verbs "block(s)/blocked" and "unblock(s)" are used generically for
  #     both card-level and customer-level actions; only the resulting STATUS
  #     value differs by entity type (see above).
  #
  # Requirement:
  #   Scenarios are tagged with the @REQ-x of the requirement they satisfy. Section
  #   numbering (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7) intentionally mirrors the source requirement
  #   document, which itself has no "section 3".
  #
  #   @REQ-1 Card-Level Blocking
  #     AC-1.1: PM Admin can temporarily block a card within their own PM scope
  #     AC-1.2: An unauthenticated actor cannot block a card
  #     AC-1.3: PM Admin cannot block a card outside their own PM scope
  #     AC-1.4: PM Admin can only apply a Temporary block, never Permanent
  #     AC-1.5: Blocking an already-Blocked card is rejected; existing block is unchanged
  #     AC-1.6: Customer portal reflects each PM's card block status independently
  #     AC-1.7: Customer cannot unblock a temporarily blocked card themselves
  #
  #   @REQ-2 Customer-Level Deactivation
  #     AC-2.1: PM Admin can temporarily deactivate a customer within their own PM scope
  #     AC-2.2: PM Admin cannot deactivate a customer belonging to another PM
  #     AC-2.3: A Deactivated customer cannot log in to that PM's customer portal
  #     AC-2.4: A Deactivated customer cannot use any card under that PM
  #     AC-2.5: A Deactivated customer cannot self-unblock, Temporary or Permanent
  #     AC-2.6: Deactivating an already-Deactivated customer is rejected; block is unchanged
  #     AC-2.7: Customer deactivation is never reversible, by anyone, regardless of type (see also @REQ-7)
  #
  #   @REQ-4 Issuer Level
  #     AC-4.1: Issuer can view a customer's cards and block status across multiple PMs
  #     AC-4.2: Issuer search for a non-existent mobile number returns no results
  #     AC-4.3: Issuer can select a PM and block specific card(s) Temporarily
  #     AC-4.4: Issuer can block specific card(s) Permanently
  #     AC-4.5: Issuer can escalate a PM-placed Temporary block to Permanent
  #     AC-4.6: Issuer can deactivate the complete customer across all PMs, Temporary or Permanent
  #     AC-4.7: Issuer can block cards across different PMs independently
  #
  #   @REQ-5 Multi-PM Isolation
  #     AC-5.1: Blocking a card under one PM does not affect cards under another PM
  #     AC-5.2: Deactivating a customer with zero cards under the acting PM succeeds, no cards affected
  #     AC-5.3: A PM Admin's customer-level deactivate only applies within that PM's own scope
  #     AC-5.4: Only an Issuer-level deactivate affects the customer across all PMs
  #
  #   @REQ-6 Portal Access for Multiple PMs
  #     AC-6.1: Customer has a separate portal login/access for each Program Manager
  #     AC-6.2: Each PM's portal displays only that PM's own cards
  #     AC-6.3: A card block under one PM is reflected only in that PM's own portal
  #     AC-6.4: Customer can still access an unaffected PM's portal normally after a block/deactivate elsewhere
  #
  #   @REQ-7 Blocking Authority
  #     AC-7.1: Only the Issuer can apply a Permanent block; PM Admin is restricted to Temporary
  #     AC-7.2: A Temporary block can be unblocked by the placing PM Admin or the Issuer
  #     AC-7.3: A Temporary block cannot be unblocked by a different PM Admin or by the customer
  #     AC-7.4: If the Issuer placed the Temporary block, only the Issuer can unblock it
  #     AC-7.5: A Permanent block can never be unblocked by anyone, including the Issuer
  #     AC-7.6: A Permanent block can never be downgraded to Temporary, by anyone
  #     AC-7.7: The customer can never unblock a card or account themselves, regardless of block type
  #     AC-7.8: Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  Background:
    Given the customer with mobile number "9937894322" exists in the system
    And the customer has 10 gift cards onboarded under "Maximize Admin"
    And the customer has 1 GPR card onboarded under "Akiko Admin"
    And all cards are currently "Active"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 0. Production Data Fix: AKIKOADMIN block must not affect MAXIMIZEADMIN
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Context: The below customers were onboarded under both AKIKOADMIN (GPR Card)
  # and MAXIMIZEADMIN (Gift Card). Per client request they were blocked under
  # AKIKOADMIN, but this incorrectly also blocked them under MAXIMIZEADMIN,
  # preventing login and Gift Card usage there. Fix: the customer must remain
  # blocked only under AKIKOADMIN and must remain/become Active under
  # MAXIMIZEADMIN. Going forward, blocking under one PM must never impact the
  # customer's status under any other PM (see also @REQ-5 Multi-PM Isolation).
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @production-fix @customer-level
  Scenario Outline: Customer blocked under AKIKOADMIN remains active and unaffected under MAXIMIZEADMIN
    Given the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" is onboarded under "Akiko Admin" with a GPR Card
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" is onboarded under "Maximize Admin" with a Gift Card
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" has been blocked under "Akiko Admin"
    And the customer with mobile number "<mobile_number>" was incorrectly also blocked under "Maximize Admin"
    When the customer's status under "Maximize Admin" is corrected to "Active"
    Then the customer status under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Blocked"
    And the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should be "Active"
    And the customer should be able to log in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    And the customer should be able to use their assigned Gift Card under "Maximize Admin" without any issues
    And the customer should not be able to log in to the "Akiko" customer portal

    Examples:
      | mobile_number |
      | 6370445590    |
      | 7718745186    |
      | 6203740710    |
      | 9768167268    |
      | 9958812998    |

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @production-fix @customer-level
  Scenario: Blocking a customer under one Program Manager must never impact their status under another Program Manager
    Given a customer is onboarded under both "Akiko Admin" and "Maximize Admin"
    When "Akiko Admin" blocks the customer within its own scope
    Then the customer status under "Akiko Admin" should be "Blocked"
    And the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"
    And the customer should be able to log in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    And the customer should be able to use any cards assigned under "Maximize Admin"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 1. Card-Level Blocking
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-1 @card-level @pm-admin
  Scenario: PM Admin blocks a card that belongs to them - block is Temporary
    Given "Akiko Admin" is logged in
    When "Akiko Admin" blocks the GPR card belonging to mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the GPR card status should be "Blocked"
    And the block type should be "Temporary"
    And the blocking authority recorded should be "Akiko Admin"
    And the 10 gift cards under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @REQ-7 @card-level @negative @auth
  Scenario: An unauthenticated actor cannot block a card
    Given no actor is logged in
    When an unauthenticated request attempts to block the GPR card belonging to mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the action should be rejected with an "authentication required" error
    And the GPR card status should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @card-level @pm-admin
  Scenario: PM Admin cannot block a card that does not belong to them
    Given "Maximize Admin" is logged in
    When "Maximize Admin" attempts to block the GPR card onboarded under "Akiko Admin"
    Then the action should be rejected with an "unauthorized card access" error
    And the GPR card status should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @REQ-7 @card-level @pm-admin @negative
  Scenario: PM Admin cannot apply a permanent block - only temporary is allowed
    Given "Akiko Admin" is logged in
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to block the GPR card with block type "Permanent"
    Then the action should be rejected with a "PM Admin can only apply temporary blocks" error
    And the GPR card status should remain "Active"

  @REQ-1 @card-level @idempotency
  Scenario: Blocking a card that is already Blocked does not change its existing block
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to block the GPR card again
    Then the action should be rejected with a "card is already blocked" message
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"
    And the GPR card block type should remain "Temporary"

  @REQ-1 @card-level @portal-access
  Scenario: Customer portal reflects mixed card statuses after a single card block
    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR card belonging to mobile number "9937894322"
    When the customer logs in to the customer portal
    Then the login should be successful
    And the "Akiko" customer portal should display 1 card as "Blocked"
    And the "Maximize" customer portal should display 10 cards as "Active"

  @REQ-1 @card-level @portal-access @negative
  Scenario: Customer cannot unblock a temporarily blocked card themselves
    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR card belonging to mobile number "9937894322"
    And the customer is logged in to the "Akiko" customer portal
    When the customer attempts to unblock the GPR card
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"
    And a message should indicate that only "Akiko Admin" or the Issuer can lift this block

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 2. Customer-Level Deactivation
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @pm-admin
  Scenario: PM Admin deactivate the complete customer via mobile number - block is Temporary
    Given "Akiko Admin" is logged in
    When "Akiko Admin" blocks the mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the customer status should be "Deactivated"
    And the block type should be "Temporary"
    And the blocking authority recorded should be "Akiko Admin"

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @pm-admin @negative
  Scenario: PM Admin cannot deactivate a customer belonging to another PM
    Given "Maximize Admin" is logged in
    When "Maximize Admin" attempts to block mobile number "9937894322" as onboarded under "Akiko Admin"
    Then the action should be rejected with an "unauthorized customer access" error
    And the customer status should remain "Active"

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @portal-access @negative
  Scenario: Deactivated customer cannot log in to that Program Manager's customer portal
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "Akiko Admin"
    When the customer attempts to log in to the "Akiko" customer portal
    Then the login should be denied
    And a message should indicate that the account is Deactivated

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @portal-access @negative
  Scenario: Deactivated customer cannot use any of their cards under that Program Manager
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "Akiko Admin"
    When any transaction is attempted on any card belonging to the customer under "Akiko Admin"
    Then the transaction should be declined
    And the decline reason should be "Customer Deactivated"

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @portal-access @negative
  Scenario: Deactivated customer cannot self-unblock their account, temporary or permanent
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "Akiko Admin"
    When the customer attempts to unblock their own account
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the customer status should remain "Deactivated"

  @REQ-2 @customer-level @idempotency
  Scenario: Deactivating a customer that is already Deactivated does not change the existing deactivate
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "Akiko Admin"
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to block mobile number "9937894322" again
    Then the action should be rejected with a "customer is already deactivated" message
    And the customer status should remain "Deactivated"
    And the customer block type should remain "Temporary"

  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 4. Issuer Level
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level
  Scenario: Issuer views a customer's cards and current block status across multiple Program Managers
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    When the Issuer searches for mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the Issuer should see the customer onboarded under 2 Program Managers:
      | Program Manager  | Card Count | Card Type  | Block Status |
      | Maximize Admin   | 10         | Gift Card  | Active       |
      | Akiko Admin      | 1          | GPR Card   | Active       |

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @negative
  Scenario: Issuer searches for a mobile number that does not exist in the system
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    When the Issuer searches for mobile number "0000000000"
    Then the search should return no results
    And a message should indicate that no customer was found for that mobile number

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @card-level
  Scenario: Issuer selects a Program Manager and blocks specific card(s) temporarily
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    And the Issuer has selected mobile number "9937894322"
    When the Issuer selects Program Manager "Maximize Admin"
    And the Issuer selects 3 of the 10 gift cards under "Maximize Admin"
    And the Issuer blocks the selected cards with block type "Temporary"
    Then those 3 gift cards should have status "Blocked"
    And the block type for those cards should be "Temporary"
    And the blocking authority recorded should be "Issuer"
    And the remaining 7 gift cards under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"
    And the GPR card under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Active"

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @card-level @permanent-block
  Scenario: Issuer blocks specific card(s) permanently
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    And the Issuer has selected mobile number "9937894322"
    When the Issuer selects Program Manager "Akiko Admin"
    And the Issuer selects the GPR card under "Akiko Admin"
    And the Issuer blocks the selected card with block type "Permanent"
    Then the GPR card should have status "Blocked"
    And the block type for the GPR card should be "Permanent"
    And the block should not be reversible by "Akiko Admin"
    And the block should not be reversible by anyone, including the Issuer

  @REQ-4 @REQ-7 @issuer-level @permanent-block
  Scenario: Issuer escalates an existing PM-placed Temporary block to Permanent
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When the Issuer changes the GPR card's block type to "Permanent"
    Then the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"
    And the GPR card block type should now be "Permanent"
    And the block should no longer be reversible by "Akiko Admin"
    And the block should not be reversible by anyone, including the Issuer

  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @customer-level
  Scenario Outline: Issuer deactivates the complete customer/mobile number across all PMs
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    And the Issuer has selected mobile number "9937894322"
    When the Issuer chooses to Deactivate the complete customer with Deactivate type "<deactivate_type>"
    Then the customer status should be "Deactivated"
    And the deactivate type should be "<deactivate_type>"
    And all 10 gift cards under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the 1 GPR card under "Akiko Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the customer should not be able to log in to any customer portal

    Examples:
| deactivate_type | block_type |
| Permanent       | Temporary  |
          
  @REQ-4 @issuer-level @card-level
  Scenario Outline: Issuer blocks cards across different Program Managers independently
    Given the Issuer is logged in
    And the Issuer has selected mobile number "9937894322"
    When the Issuer selects Program Manager "<program_manager>"
    And the Issuer blocks all cards under "<program_manager>"
    Then all cards under "<program_manager>" should have status "Blocked"
    And all cards under "<other_program_manager>" should remain "Active"

    Examples:
      | program_manager | other_program_manager |
      | Maximize Admin  | Akiko Admin            |
      | Akiko Admin     | Maximize Admin         |


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 5. Multi-PM Isolation Rule
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation
  Scenario: Blocking a card under one PM does not affect cards under another PM
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894322"
    And "Akiko Admin" manages 1 card for the same mobile number
    When "Maximize Admin" blocks one of its 10 gift cards
    Then that card under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the remaining 9 cards under "Maximize Admin" should remain "Active"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Active"
    And "Akiko Admin" should be able to continue normal operations on its card

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @edge-case
  Scenario: Deactivating a customer who has no cards onboarded under the acting PM succeeds with zero cards affected
    Given the customer with mobile number "9937894300" exists in the system
    And the customer has 0 cards onboarded under "Maximize Admin"
    When "Maximize Admin" deactivates the customer within its own scope
    Then the customer status under "Maximize Admin" should be "Deactivated"
    And no cards should be affected, since none exist under "Maximize Admin"

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @customer-level
  Scenario: Customer-level deactivate by one PM only applies within that PM's scope
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894300"
    And "Akiko Admin" manages 1 card for the same mobile number
    When "Maximize Admin" deactivates the customer within its own scope
    Then all 10 cards under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should remain "Active"
    And "Akiko Admin" should be able to continue normal operations on its card

  @REQ-5 @multi-pm @isolation @issuer-level
  Scenario: Only an Issuer-level deactivate affects the customer across all PMs
    Given "Maximize Admin" manages 10 cards for mobile number "9937894322"
    And "Akiko Admin" manages 1 card for the same mobile number
    When the Issuer deactivates the complete customer/mobile number
    Then all 10 cards under "Maximize Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the 1 card under "Akiko Admin" should have status "Blocked"
    And the customer should not be able to log in to the customer portal


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 6. Customer Portal Access for Multiple Program Managers
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm
  Scenario: Customer has separate portal logins for each Program Manager
    Given the customer is onboarded under both "Maximize Admin" and "Akiko Admin"
    When the customer's portal accounts are provisioned
    Then the customer should have a separate login/access for the "Maximize" customer portal
    And the customer should have a separate login/access for the "Akiko" customer portal

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm
  Scenario: Akiko portal only shows cards associated with Akiko
    When the customer logs in to the "Akiko" customer portal
    Then the portal should display only 1 card, the GPR Card
    And the portal should not display any of the 10 Gift Cards from "Maximize"

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm
  Scenario: Maximize portal only shows cards associated with Maximize
    When the customer logs in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    Then the portal should display only the 10 Gift Cards
    And the portal should not display the GPR Card from "Akiko"

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm @card-level
  Scenario: A card blocked under Akiko is reflected in the Akiko portal
    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR Card
    When the customer logs in to the "Akiko" customer portal
    Then the portal should display the GPR Card with status "Blocked"

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm @card-level
  Scenario: A card blocked under Akiko does not affect the Maximize portal
    Given "Akiko Admin" has blocked the GPR Card
    When the customer logs in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    Then the portal should display all 10 Gift Cards with status "Active"

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm @isolation
  Scenario: Customer can still access the unaffected PM's portal normally after a deactivate elsewhere
    Given the GPR Card under "Akiko" has been blocked
    When the customer logs in to the "Maximize" customer portal
    Then the login should be successful
    And all 10 Gift Cards should be displayed with status "Active"
    And none of the Gift Cards should be affected by the "Akiko" block

  @REQ-6 @portal-access @multi-pm
  Scenario Outline: Each Program Manager's portal reflects only that PM's card status
    Given "<pm>" card status is "<status>"
    When the customer logs in to the "<pm>" customer portal
    Then the portal should display the "<pm>" card(s) with status "<status>"
    And the portal should not display or be influenced by any other Program Manager's card status

    Examples:
      | pm       | status  |
      | Akiko    | Blocked |
      | Maximize | Active  |


  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # 7. Blocking Authority: who can BLOCK vs who can UNBLOCK
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------
  # Block placement rule:
  #   - PM Admin can only ever place a "Temporary" block (card or customer level),
  #     and only for cards/customers within their own PM's scope.
  #   - Issuer can place either a "Temporary" or a "Permanent" block/deactivate (card or customer
  #     level), and may escalate an existing Temporary block to Permanent.
  #
  # Unblock rule:
  #   - Temporary block:
  #       -> can be unblocked by the SAME PM Admin who placed it, OR by the Issuer.
  #       -> cannot be unblocked by a different PM Admin, or by the customer.
  #       -> if the Issuer placed the temporary block, only the Issuer can unblock it
  #          (a PM Admin cannot undo an Issuer-placed block).
  #   - Permanent block (Issuer only):
  #       -> can NEVER be unblocked by anyone, including the Issuer.
  #   - The customer can NEVER unblock anything themselves, regardless of level or
  #     block type.
  #   - Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op.
  #   - Customer/mobile-number deactivation is NEVER reversible, regardless of
  #     deactivate type (Temporary or Permanent) or who attempts it (PM Admin or
  #     Issuer). This differs from card-level temporary blocks, which ARE reversible
  #     by the placing PM Admin or the Issuer. Do not assume the card unblock
  #     pattern carries over to customer-level deactivation.
  # ---------------------------------------------------------------------

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario Outline: Only the Issuer can apply a permanent block; PM Admin is restricted to temporary
    Given "<actor>" is logged in
    When "<actor>" attempts to block "<target>" with block type "<block_type>"
    Then the action should be "<result>"

    Examples:
      | actor          | target            | block_type | result   |
      | Akiko Admin    | a card            | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Akiko Admin    | a card            | Permanent  | Rejected |
      | Maximize Admin | complete customer | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Maximize Admin | complete customer | Permanent  | Rejected |
      | Issuer         | a card            | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | a card            | Permanent  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | complete customer | Temporary  | Allowed  |
      | Issuer         | complete customer | Permanent  | Allowed  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario Outline: A card temporarily blocked by Akiko Admin can be unblocked by Akiko Admin or the Issuer
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "<actor>" unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should be "Active"

    Examples:
      | actor       |
      | Akiko Admin |
      | Issuer      |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: A card temporarily blocked by Akiko Admin cannot be unblocked by anyone else
    Given "Akiko Admin" has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to unblock the GPR card
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | attempted_by              |
      | Maximize Admin            |
      | the customer (via portal) |

  @REQ-2 @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: A deactivated customer can never be reactivated, regardless of deactivate type or who attempts it
    Given mobile number "9937894322" has been Deactivated by "<deactivated_by>" with deactivate type "<deactivate_type>"
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to reactivate mobile number "9937894322"
    Then the action should be rejected with a "customer deactivation cannot be reversed" error
    And the customer status should remain "Deactivated"

    Examples:
      | deactivated_by | deactivate_type | attempted_by |
      | Akiko Admin    | Temporary       | Akiko Admin  |
      | Akiko Admin    | Temporary       | Issuer       |
      | Issuer         | Permanent       | Issuer       |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario: A PM Admin cannot unblock a card that the Issuer temporarily blocked
    Given the Issuer has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When "Akiko Admin" attempts to unblock the GPR card
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And the GPR card status should remain "Blocked"

  @REQ-7 @block-authority
  Scenario: The Issuer can unblock a card that the Issuer temporarily blocked
    Given the Issuer has temporarily blocked the GPR card
    When the Issuer unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should be "Active"

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative @permanent-block
  Scenario Outline: A permanently blocked card or customer can never be unblocked by anyone
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is permanently blocked by the Issuer
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to unblock "<target>"
    Then the unblock action should be denied
    And "<target>" should remain permanently "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | target             | attempted_by |
      | a single card      | Issuer       |
      | a single card      | Akiko Admin  |
      | a single card      | the customer |
      | complete customer  | Issuer       |
      | complete customer  | Akiko Admin  |
      | complete customer  | the customer |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative
  Scenario Outline: The customer can never unblock a card or account themselves, regardless of block type
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is "Blocked" with block type "<block_type>"
    And the customer is logged in to the relevant customer portal
    When the customer attempts to unblock "<target>"
    Then the unblock action should be denied in all cases

    Examples:
      | target             | block_type |
      | a single card      | Temporary  |
      | a single card      | Permanent  |
      | complete customer  | Temporary  |
      | complete customer  | Permanent  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @negative @permanent-block
  Scenario Outline: A permanent block can never be downgraded to Temporary by anyone, including the Issuer
    Given "<target>" belonging to mobile number "9937894322" is permanently blocked by the Issuer
    When "<attempted_by>" attempts to change "<target>" block type to "Temporary"
    Then the action should be rejected with a "permanent block cannot be reversed" error
    And "<target>" should remain permanently "Blocked"

    Examples:
      | target             | attempted_by |
      | a single card      | Issuer       |
      | a single card      | Akiko Admin  |
      | complete customer  | Issuer       |
      | complete customer  | Akiko Admin  |

  @REQ-7 @block-authority @idempotency @edge-case
  Scenario: Unblocking a card that is already Active is a safe no-op
    Given the GPR card status is "Active"
    When "Akiko Admin" unblocks the GPR card
    Then the GPR card status should remain "Active"
    And no error should be raised
